To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) insulin resistance is a major cause of obesity, (2) obesity is a major cause, or at least a major contributor, to hypertension, and (3) the mechanisms of obesity-induced hypertension involve insulin resistance and increased sympathetic nervous system activity.
obesity is associated with insulin resistance and that insulin resistance is associated with sympathetic overactivity.
insulin and the autonomic nervous system are involved in the regulation of energy balance, and that these systems may be involved in the development of hypertension in the obese.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms by which insulin and the sympathetic system regulate energy balance.
the role of insulin and the sympathetic system in the control of energy balance and body weight, and the relationship of this to the development of hypertension.

the following hypotheses: (1) obesity and hypertension may be linked by insulin and the sympathetic adrenomedullary system; (2) insulin and sympathetic nervous system activity may influence blood pressure through their effects on renal sodium handling; (3) the hypertension associated with obesity is an adaptive response to limit weight gain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
obesity is associated with hypertension in a dose-dependent manner.
the hypertension of overweight is the unfortunate by-product, or side-effect, of a physiological mechanism that is designed to maintain a constant body weight.
obesity is not a disease, but a condition that can be associated with a number of diseases, and in some cases, may be a cause of these diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

insulin is a major regulator of sympathetic nervous system activity, and that the sympathetic nervous system regulates energy metabolism, and that the regulation of sympathetic activity by insulin is important to energy metabolism.
the obesity of the modern world may be the unfortunate result of a mismatch between the energy balance mechanisms of the human body and the environment in which we live.
obesity and hypertension are linked by a common cause, the overconsumption of calories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the obesity-hypertension link is a result of the body's attempts to regulate energy balance, and that this link is mediated by insulin.
the obesity-hypertension association is not a chance occurrence but rather a consequence of the body’s attempt to defend itself against excess weight gain.
we have identified a new mechanism that can explain how insulin resistance leads to obesity and hypertension.
